title: The Eight Emotions
paragraphs: When Pūmpukār had been recreated With beauty and splendour blending, With art and artist at their best, At a function marked by grandeur, In the assembly of poets celebrating Tamil The lines I recited from my poem I recall And make them a beautiful archway to Tolkāppiyam Meyppāṭṭiyal.
The eight kinds of manifest emotions treated therein are: Laughter, grief, disgust, wonder Fear, pride, anger and joy.
By treading the path shown by The father of grammar in Tamil, Let us happily relish the eight sentiments: Laughter, grief, disgust, wonder, Fear, pride, anger and joy.
I say This section on sentiments does really transport us to ecstasy.

Laughter is what emerges when we obstinately work at a person given to fear. The valiant are astonished at people who are not infuriated by humiliation. Happiness and weeping are the children of the same mother.

> For us to be served to the fill > These > Eight sentiments > In Tamil > Like curd delicious, > We shall further see > In the ‘blossoms’ succeeding > The way Tolkāppiyar, > Who was hailed > By poets of threefold Tamil > In the courts of > The crowned monarchs > Where fluttered > The silken banner > Aloft the royal canopy, > Looks at them.
> These eight kinds of manifest emotions are > Laughter, grief, disgust, wonder > Fear, pride, anger and joy.
